items.new_text: A test of the test harness itself can declare that it is infrastructure and proves no requirement; the finishing gate then accepts it without a requirement tag, only when its file is on a pre-approved list that existed before the change, and never counts it toward requirement coverage

Given a test of the test harness itself proves no product requirement, when its author declares it as infrastructure ("tooling" or "infra") in its own source and its file is named exactly in the pre-approved list as that list stood before the change, then the finishing gate counts it as infrastructure instead of demanding a requirement tag; it never counts toward requirement coverage, the gate reports how many tests were classed this way, a declaration the gate cannot honour (unlisted file, a requirement tag as well, siblings that disagree, or a correction that would leave a requirement without a test) is refused, and a list edited in the same change licenses nothing. A module-level declaration classes only the tests already in its file: a test added later needs its own declaration, and a real requirement test cannot live in such a file.
